Let the speed of each train be V meter per second.
Let the lengths of the two trains be L1 and L2.
Now, the important concept here is when a train crosses a pole,
it covers only its own length.
There is no platform or another train involved.
So the distance covered is simply the length of the train.
Hence, we use the formula speed equals length of train divided by time.
Since both trains have the same speed, this speed will be equal for both.
So we can say speed of first train equals L1 by time taken by first train,
